Archived: this article describes the classic interface, retired in March 2025.
See the current article for the new layout.
In classic Harbour CRM, contacts were added from the old Contacts tab.
Click the Contacts tab on the left-hand menu.
Click the green Add Contact button above the list.
Fill in First Name, Last Name and Email in the pop-up window.
Click Save & Close, or Save & Add Another to enter several people in a row.
In the classic version the Company field was a plain text box, so linked companies had to be matched later by an administrator.
Update a contact's phone number (classic)
edit phone in old contact page
change customer phone, classic editor
classic contact edit
Archived: describes the classic editor, retired in March 2025.
To change a contact's phone number in the classic editor:
Open the old Contacts tab and click the contact's name.
Click Edit Contact in the grey toolbar.
Find the Phone (Primary) box and type the new number.
Classic did not add country codes automatically, so include the + sign.
Click Update.
A second number could be stored in Phone (Alt).
Changes were not logged in the contact's history in the classic version, which is why some older accounts have no record of who edited a number.
Change a contact's email (classic)
edit contact email old interface
update customer email classic
old contacts tab email
Archived: this article describes the classic interface, retired in March 2025.
Open the old Contacts tab.
Click the contact, then Edit Contact.
Type the new address into the Email box.
Classic accepted only one address per contact.
Click Update.
If the old address was on a mailing list, you also needed to open Lists and remove it by hand, because classic did not sync the two.
Duplicate email warnings did not exist, so two contacts could share the same address without any message.
Delete a contact (classic)
remove contact old Contacts tab
classic delete customer
permanently delete a contact
Archived: classic interface, retired in March 2025.
Deleting a contact in the classic version was immediate and could not be reversed.
Open the old Contacts tab.
Tick the box beside one or more contacts.
Click Actions > Delete Selected.
Click OK on the grey warning box.
No recycle bin existed.
Any open deals showed the contact name in plain text but were no longer linked.
Classic accounts needed to contact support within 7 days to ask for a backup restore, a policy that no longer applies.
Export contacts to CSV (classic)
download contact list old version
classic export
export customers legacy
Archived: describes the classic export, retired in March 2025.
Click the Contacts tab.
Click Tools in the top right and choose Export to CSV.
Classic always exported every contact and every column; there was no filter.
Click Generate File.
A link appeared under Tools > My Downloads after a few minutes and stayed for 48 hours.
Custom fields were placed at the end of the file with their internal names, such as cf_1042, rather than their labels.
Exports were limited to 10,000 rows.
Link a contact to a company (classic)

classic company link
old Contacts tab company
Archived: classic interface, retired in March 2025.
In classic, the link between a contact and a company was set from the company side.
Open the Accounts tab (the old name for Companies).
Click the company name.
Scroll to Related Contacts and click Link Existing.
Tick one or more contacts and click Add.
The Company box on the contact page was only a text label and did not create a link.
Today you can link directly from the contact's page.
Add a company (classic Accounts tab)
create account in old CRM
new company classic
add an organisation old UI
Archived: this article describes the classic interface, retired in March 2025.
Companies were called Accounts in the classic version.
Click the Accounts tab.
Click New Account.
Type the Account Name.
Also fill in Phone, Web and Billing Street if you have them.
Choose an Account Owner from the drop-down.
Classic had no website lookup.
Logos could only be uploaded manually on the edit page.
Edit a company's phone, website or address (classic)
change account phone old
update company address classic
edit Accounts tab

Open the Accounts tab and click the company.
Click Edit in the grey toolbar.
Change Phone, Web or the address fields Street, City, State and Postcode.
Each part of the address was a separate box.
The website was not checked, so entries like www.example needed the full http:// to be clickable.
Contacts linked to the account did not pick up the new address; they had their own address fields.
Create a deal (classic pipeline)
add opportunity old CRM
new deal classic
create sales deal old interface
Archived: describes the classic pipeline, retired in March 2025.
Click the Pipeline tab.
Click + Add Opportunity at the top of the first column.
Enter the Opportunity Name and Value.
Search for the Contact.
The company is filled in from the contact.

The Close Date was optional, which meant reports often showed gaps.

classic deal status
set opportunity to lost

In the Pipeline tab, click the opportunity card.
Click Change Status.
Choose Closed Won or Closed Lost.
For Closed Lost, type a reason in the free-text Notes box.
Classic had no reason list.
Closed cards disappeared from the board and could only be found by filtering the list view with Show Closed.
There was no Reopen button; support had to reopen them.
Move a deal to another stage (classic Kanban)
drag opportunity old pipeline
change stage classic
advance opportunity
Archived: this article describes the classic Kanban board, retired in March 2025.
Open the Pipeline tab.
Click and hold the opportunity card.
Drag it onto the next column header and release.
A box asks for a Stage Note.
Click Skip if not needed.
On laptops without a mouse, open the card, click Edit and use the Stage drop-down instead.
Classic could not skip over locked stages, and there was no keyboard method.

add custom field old settings
classic custom fields

Click the cog icon, then Settings > Legacy > Field Manager.
Choose the module: Contacts, Accounts or Opportunities.
Click Create Field.
Enter a Field Name and choose a Data Type: Text, Number, Date or Pick List.

New fields only showed on records after the user refreshed the browser.

edit custom field name old
change field label legacy
classic Field Manager

Go to Settings > Legacy > Field Manager.
Select the module and find the field.
Click the Edit link at the end of the row.
Change the Field Name.
Renaming in classic did not update saved reports or filters that used the old name; they showed an empty column until someone rebuilt them.
This limitation is the reason many clients kept the old name and added a description instead.

remove field Settings Legacy
classic delete field

Open Settings > Legacy > Field Manager.
Find the field for the right module.
Click Delete at the end of the row.
Click Yes, delete on the warning.
Values were wiped immediately from every record and could not be restored.
Deleting a field used by a saved report caused that report to show an error until it was edited.
Only users with the Super Admin role could delete fields in classic.
Change your client contact number (classic account page)
update our business phone old settings
classic My Account phone
company phone legacy account
Archived: classic interface, retired in March 2025.
In classic Harbour CRM, the client is the business using the CRM, and its number was kept on the old My Account page.
Click your name at the top right and choose My Account.
Open the Company Profile section.
Edit Primary Phone.
Click Update Profile.
Changes needed a support ticket if the account had more than one Super Admin.
No verification code was sent.
This number is different from any contact's phone number.
Change the billing email (classic)
update invoice email for subscription old
classic billing contact
old My Account billing
Archived: describes the classic interface, retired in March 2025.
Click your name and choose My Account.
Open Plan & Billing.
Click Change next to Invoice Email.
Enter the new address and click Save.
In classic the receipts for the whole account went to this single address, and there was no confirmation link.
Because of that, some accounts discovered missed receipts months later.
The newer Billing page supports additional recipients and a verification email.
Change currency (classic Settings > Legacy)
switch currency old CRM
legacy currency setting
default currency classic
Archived: classic interface, retired in March 2025.
Go to Settings > Legacy > Localisation.
Choose a value from Base Currency.
Changing the base currency in classic recalculated every opportunity value using that day's exchange rate, which surprised many clients.
This is no longer the behaviour: amounts are left unchanged.
Classic also required you to log out and back in before the new currency symbol appeared.
Reset your password (classic sign-in page)
forgot password old login
classic password reset
can't sign in old
Archived: describes the classic sign-in page, retired in March 2025.
On the old sign-in page, click Trouble signing in? under the password box.
Type your username.
In classic this was often not your email address.
Click Email Me.
Follow the link, which expired after 24 hours, and enter a password of at least 8 characters.
Passwords from classic were accepted without symbols or numbers.
Everyone has since been asked to update to the newer 12-character rule.
Lead scoring (retired feature)
score my leads
lead score points
rate contacts automatically
Archived: this feature was retired in March 2025 along with the classic interface.
Lead scoring gave each contact a number of points based on activity.
Go to Settings > Legacy > Scoring Rules.
Click New Rule.
Choose an event such as Email opened (+2) or Form submitted (+10).
Click Save Rule.
Scores appeared in a Score column on the old Contacts tab.
Existing scores were not carried over to the new interface.
Use deal stages and tags to prioritise contacts instead.
Data retention policy for deleted records (pre-2025)
how long are deleted contacts kept
old retention period
deleted data backups
Archived: superseded policy.
Retention changed after March 2025.
Under the previous policy, records deleted from your Harbour CRM were kept in system backups for 7 days and then removed.
During that period, the client's account owner could ask support to restore them.
Requests had to be made from the client's registered billing email, and restoration was a full-account restore, not a single contact.
Because of that, anything created after the backup time was lost.
This policy does not apply to accounts migrated to the new interface.
Please see the current article on deleting contacts for the timeframes that apply today.
Import contacts (classic importer)
upload CSV to old CRM
classic import wizard
import customers legacy
Archived: classic importer, retired in March 2025.
Click Tools > Import Contacts.
Click Choose File and select a CSV.
XLSX files were not supported.
Click Next and match each column header to a field.
Headers had to match exactly or be mapped by hand.
Click Run Import.
Classic created a duplicate whenever an email already existed, and there was no undo.
The recommended trick was to export first, then import into a test account.
Imports over 5,000 rows were split by support.
Using the Tasks tab (retired)
to-do list in old CRM
follow-up reminders classic
Tasks tab
Archived: the Tasks tab was retired in March 2025.
In the classic interface, follow-ups were kept in a separate Tasks tab.
Click Tasks in the left menu.
Click New Task.
Type a Subject, choose a Due Date and link the task to a contact with Related To.
Overdue tasks were shown in red.
Tasks are now created from the contact or deal itself under Activities, and existing tasks were migrated automatically.
Recurring tasks were not supported in classic.
Generate a legacy API key
old API token
classic API access
create API key old settings
Archived: legacy API keys stopped working in June 2025.
Click the cog icon and choose Settings > Legacy > API Access.
Click Generate Key.
Copy the key immediately.
It was shown only once.
Use it as the X-Harbour-Key header on your requests.
Legacy keys had full access to everything in the client's account and could not be limited.
They have been replaced by scoped tokens.
Anyone still using an old key must create a new token and update their connected tools.
Two-step sign-in by text message (retired)
SMS verification code
text message login code
old two factor
Archived: SMS codes were retired in March 2025 for security reasons.
Classic accounts could receive a six-digit code by text message.
Open My Account > Security.
Click Enable Text Verification.
Enter your mobile number and click Send Code.
Type the code and click Confirm.
The number used was the sign-in user's own mobile, not the client contact number in company settings.
If you still see this setting, switch to an authenticator app as described in the current security articles.
Update an employee's phone number (classic)
change staff phone old People
edit employee mobile classic
legacy staff directory
Archived: describes the classic People directory, retired in 2025.
Click Staff Directory in the left menu.
Click the employee's name.
Click the Edit pencil on the Contact Info card.
Change Mobile or Work Phone.
In the classic version only the HR Admin role could change numbers; employees saw their own details as read-only.
Numbers were shown in the staff directory to everyone, a setting that is now optional.
Request leave (classic form)
book time off old People
apply for annual leave classic
old leave form
Archived: classic leave form, retired in 2025.
Click My Leave and then Request Leave.
Pick a Leave Type from the list.
Type the From and To dates in DD/MM/YYYY format.
Add a reason in the Comments box.
Click Submit Request.
Your manager received an email with Approve and Decline links.
Half days could only be entered by writing 0.5 in the Days box.
The calendar view did not exist in classic.
Add an employee (classic wizard)
new starter old People
create staff record legacy
onboard employee classic
Archived: the three-step wizard was retired in 2025.
Click Staff Directory then Add Employee.
Step 1: enter Name, Email and Start Date.
Step 2: choose Department and Manager.
Step 3: tick the Welcome email box if you want the invitation sent.
Click Finish.
Bank details and tax numbers could not be entered at this point; they were added later by a second administrator.
The new onboarding checklist replaces this process.
Send an invoice reminder (classic)
chase unpaid invoice old
overdue notice classic
payment reminder legacy
Archived: describes the classic invoice list, retired in 2025.
Click Sales > Invoice List.
Tick the overdue invoices, shown with a red date.
Click Send Reminder.
A fixed message is shown.
The text could only be edited by an administrator in Settings > Legacy > Email Text.
Reminders could not be scheduled in advance.
Customers saw a plain email with the invoice attached as a PDF and no online payment link.
Create an invoice (classic editor)
make a new invoice old editor
classic invoice form
raise invoice legacy
Archived: classic invoice editor, retired in 2025.
Click Sales > New Invoice.
Choose the customer from the Bill To drop-down.
Click Add Line for each product or service and enter Description, Qty and Price.
Tick Tax Inclusive if prices already include tax.
Click Save Draft or Approve & Send.
The classic editor had no autosave, so closing the window lost your work.
Invoice numbers could not be changed after approval.
Refund policy for Harbour Invoicing payments (old)
refund customer payment old
how long do refunds take previously
payment refunds policy
Archived: superseded policy, replaced January 2025.
Under the earlier policy, refunds of card payments taken through Harbour Invoicing had to be requested by raising a ticket with support, and only the full amount could be returned.
Refunds took up to 10 working days and the processing fee on the original payment was not returned.
Clients can now issue full or partial refunds themselves from the payment record, and the fee treatment is described in the current pricing terms.
This article is kept for audit purposes and should not be used to answer current questions.
Change invoice currency (classic)
old invoice currency setting
switch currency legacy invoicing
default currency classic invoice
Archived: describes Settings > Legacy, retired in 2025.
Click the cog icon and choose Settings > Legacy > Business.
Open the Currency drop-down.
Pick the currency and click Save.
Classic only allowed one currency per account, so every invoice, quote and statement changed at once.
Invoices that were already approved kept their old symbol on the PDF but showed the new one on screen, which caused confusion.
Create a separate account if you needed to bill in two currencies.
Create an email campaign (Classic editor)
send a newsletter old editor
classic campaign builder
make mass email legacy
Archived: describes the Classic editor, retired in March 2025.
Click Campaigns > Create and choose Classic Editor.
Type a Campaign Name and Subject.
Select a list under Send To.
In the editor, use the toolbar to add text, images and buttons.
Layouts were chosen from six fixed templates.
Click Send Test, then Schedule or Send Now.
The classic editor did not preview on mobile screens.
Segments were not available; you had to build a separate list.
Add a subscriber (classic lists)
add someone to mailing list old
subscribe contact manually legacy
classic list members
Archived: classic Lists screen, retired in March 2025.
Click Lists and then the name of your list.
Click Add Subscriber.
Type the Email Address and, if you like, First Name.
Tick They have given permission to continue.
Subscribers added by hand were marked as Manual.
Classic could not import from Harbour CRM contacts; you had to export and upload a CSV.
The sync introduced in the new version removes that step.
Set up a sender domain (legacy DNS wizard)
authenticate email domain old
SPF DKIM setup classic
verify domain Mail
Archived: legacy wizard retired in 2025.
Go to Settings > Legacy > Sender Domains.
Click Add Domain and type yours.
Copy the two TXT records shown and add them in your DNS host.
Click Check Records.
Verification could take up to 48 hours.
The wizard used a shared signing key, so reputation was shared with other clients.
The current setup provides a unique key for each domain and lists the records with copy buttons.
Assign a ticket (classic Desk)
give ticket to agent old
reassign ticket classic
legacy ticket owner
Archived: describes the classic Desk inbox, retired in 2025.
Click Inbox and open the ticket.
In the header click the Owner name.
Choose an agent from the list.
Teams were not available as owners.
Click Set Owner.
The agent was not told unless you ticked Notify by email.
Assigning several tickets at once was done from the list with Select All and Change Owner, which applied to every ticket on the page, including ones you did not mean to select.
Create a ticket on behalf of a customer (classic)
log a support request old Desk
new ticket classic
open case manually
Archived: classic Desk, retired in 2025.
Click New Case at the top of the Inbox.
Type the customer's email under Requester.
Enter a Subject and describe the issue.
Choose a Priority (Low, Normal or Urgent).
Click Create & Close or Create & Open.
Cases were the classic name for tickets.
Attachments were limited to 5 MB.
Customers did not receive a copy unless Email requester was ticked.
Service level targets (old policy)
response time targets
SLA timers previously
first reply time old
Archived: superseded, replaced in 2025.
Under the previous setup, Harbour Desk used one account-wide first-reply target.
Go to Settings > Legacy > Targets and enter a number of hours.
The clock ran 24 hours a day, including weekends, and was not paused when a ticket was waiting for the customer.
Breached cases turned red in the Inbox.
Business hours and separate targets by priority are now supported, so this article should not be used to describe how timers work today.

start new project old interface
classic project setup
legacy project creation

Click Projects then Start Project.
Enter a Title and Description.
Pick a Project Type: Standard or Template-based.
Select members from the Team list.
Click Create.
Classic opened the project on the List tab; boards were added later.
Colours and icons did not exist.
The Client Access option shown in some older screenshots has been removed.

new task old Projects
create to-do classic
legacy task form
Archived: classic task list, retired in 2025.
Open the project and click the Tasks tab.
Click + Task at the bottom of the list.
Type the Task Name and press Enter.
Click the row to open the side panel and set Assignee and Due.
Classic did not allow sub-tasks, and an assignee could only be one person.
To split work, users created several tasks with similar names, which made reports hard to read.

Click Actions > Close Project.
Choose whether to Keep tasks visible or Hide tasks.
Click Confirm.
Closed projects were moved to the Closed tab.
They could be reopened only by a Project Admin.
Time entries could not be added after closing, so unbilled hours had to be logged first.

Select Edit in the top right corner.

From the board view:
Open Deals and choose Board.
Drag the deal card into the next column.
From the deal page:
Open the deal.
Select the stage name at the top, then pick a new stage from the list.
Moving a deal records the change in its timeline.
Some stages may ask for extra details, such as a Next step.

Go to Settings > Custom fields.
Select the record type: Contacts, Companies or Deals.
Choose Add field.
Enter a Label and pick a Field type such as Text, Number, Date or Dropdown.
